issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to manage shared stock, but the solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. The template's Main (commented) also refers to acceptSupplyDelivery. This name/signature mismatch between specification/template and solution will confuse students and cause tests expecting acceptSupplyDelivery to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the static method name in the implementation match the specification: rename receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same parameters (String name, int price, int quantity), or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery. Ensure the method is static on SealSaloon to match the problem statement and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the commented example in Main) require a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon to handle deliveries, but the solution implements this functionality with a differently named static method receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery into the shared stock) creates a mapping burden: students reading the problem and template will look for acceptSupplyDelivery while the reference solution uses receiveDelivery, and tests or example code may call acceptSupplyDelivery. The name divergence is not an intentional pedagogical variation and can lead to confusion and failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Rename SealSaloon.receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (keep it static) and update any call sites. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template examples to reference receiveDelivery, but prefer using acceptSupplyDelivery to match the original specification and tests.
